ai.title: Context Pruner Agent Added
ai.summary: New `context-pruner` agent added to `.agents/` to reduce token usage by pruning old tool results and messages before each step. Base agent updated to spawn this inline via `spawn_agent_inline` in `factory/base.ts`. CI workflows and root `package.json` updated to include `.agents` in test matrices. `tool-renderers.ts` modified to suppress UI output for `spawn_agent_inline`.

eli5.text: The AI assistant now automatically cleans out old information from its memory before moving on to each new step, so it can work faster and avoid hitting its memory limit. It does this by quietly removing the oldest tool results and messages it no longer needs, without showing you extra output or popping up new windows. This runs automatically whenever you use an agent, including the standard coding assistant, and you wouldn't see any visible change in the interface except that long sessions are less likely to get cut off. The change also adds test coverage so this cleanup behavior won't accidentally break in the future.

ai.title: codebuff 1.0.468
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.468 in npm-app/release/package.json. No code changes.

eli5.text: The version number for the CodeBuff AI assistant was bumped up, and this release brings a mix of smaller fixes and a few more notable capabilities. If you updated to this version, you'd get improvements like better handling of agent instructions, clearer documentation about how agents are defined, and some behind-the-scenes changes to how the assistant connects to external AI services. A couple of the changes relate to a new "context-pruner" agent and improvements to how reasoning is handled for agents, which means agents can now be configured more precisely for different levels of thinking depth. Overall, nothing huge changed in terms of user-facing features, but it's a maintenance update that keeps the system running smoothly and sets up some groundwork for future capabilities.

ai.title: Filter reasoning tokens when exclude flag set
ai.summary: Removed hardcoded `includeReasoning: true` from OpenRouter language model config. Added logic in `promptAiSdkStream` to skip `reasoning-delta` chunks if `options.providerOptions?.openrouter?.reasoning?.exclude` is true. Imported `OpenRouterProviderOptions` type in `backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts`. Ensures reasoning tokens are manually stripped when exclusion is requested.

eli5.text: When an assistant answers you through OpenRouter, it sometimes thinks out loud, producing extra internal reasoning tokens before its visible reply. Developers previously couldn't turn that off, so those hidden thinking tokens always came through. Now, when a developer sets a flag asking to exclude reasoning, those internal thinking chunks are filtered out during streaming instead of being sent. If you looked at the settings, you would simply see a new option to hide the model's internal chain-of-thought reasoning.

ai.title: Fix agent cache key mismatch in agent-registry
ai.summary: Agent template caching in `backend/src/templates/agent-registry.ts` now uses `dbAgent.id` as the cache key instead of the requested `agentId`. This ensures cache hits only occur when the stored agent ID matches the lookup key, preventing potential mismatches or stale data retrieval. The change applies to both Codebuff-parsed and standard published agent fetches.

eli5.text: When the system looks up a saved assistant by name, it now uses the assistant's own unique ID to find what's already been fetched instead of the name you typed in. This means you'll reliably get back the exact version that was stored, rather than a possible mismatch from a differently-named lookup. It's a behind-the-scenes fix that prevents the cache from returning stale or incorrect data.

ai.title: Fix spawn-agent-inline version matching
ai.summary: Refactors spawn-agent-inline to use getMatchingSpawn for resolving agent types against parentAgentTemplate.spawnableAgents. Replaces direct string inclusion checks with version-aware matching logic. Ensures spawned agents correctly resolve to their specific template versions rather than failing on strict type equality. Updates backend/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-agent-inline.ts.

eli5.text: When one AI helper spawns a sub-helper inside the same session, it now picks the right matching version of that sub-helper instead of demanding an exact type name. If you use these nested helpers, the system will stop rejecting valid sub-helpers that were previously blocked by overly strict name checks. The change is live today for anyone running spawn-agent-inline workflows.

ai.title: Refactor spawn agent handlers with shared utils and tests
ai.summary: Consolidates duplicated validation and execution logic from `spawn-agents.ts`, `spawn-agents-async.ts`, and `spawn-agent-inline.ts` into a new `spawn-agent-utils.ts` module. Functions like `validateSpawnState`, `validateAndGetAgentTemplate`, and `executeAgent` are extracted to reduce code redundancy and ensure consistent error handling across spawn modes. Adds `spawn-agents-permissions.test.ts` to cover permission checks. Scope limited to backend tool handlers.

eli5.text: Three different ways the assistant starts up a helper agent (inline, async, and regular spawn) used to each carry their own copy of the same checks and setup steps, so fixing a bug in one place often left the other two still broken. The shared checklist and setup work have been pulled into one common helper, and a new test file now checks that permission rules are enforced consistently across all three startup paths. Nothing visible changed for how you start a helper agent, but future fixes or new safety checks now apply to every startup method at once instead of needing to be copied three times.

ai.title: Prefer spawnagents over spawnagentinline
ai.summary: Agent base prompts now explicitly mandate `spawn_agents` and forbid `spawn_agent_inline` unless specified. `spawn_agent-inline.ts` tool description adds guidance to reserve inline spawning for special cases. Scope limited to `.agents/prompts/base-prompts.ts` and `backend/src/tools/definitions/tool/spawn-agent-inline.ts`. Mechanism relies on prompt steering to reduce context bloat from inline message history preservation.

eli5.text: When the system decides to bring in a specialized helper to work on part of your request, it will now use the standard handoff method instead of the inline method. The inline method keeps the helper's work embedded in the current conversation thread, which adds more content that needs to be tracked. The standard handoff is lighter, so the overall process runs more efficiently. If you were watching closely, you might notice slightly faster or cleaner handoffs between assistants, though most people won't see a visible difference.

ai.title: Add maxContextLength parameter to agent context pruning
ai.summary: Introduced a `maxContextLength` parameter to the input schema for `context-pruner` and `base` agents. This allows dynamic configuration of the token limit, replacing the previous hardcoded 200,000 token threshold. The `base` agent factory now forwards this parameter to the `context-pruner` during inline spawning. This change affects internal agent definitions in `.agents/context-pruner.ts` and `.agents/factory/base.ts`.

eli5.text: The internal pruning tool that trims an assistant's memory can now be told a specific size limit instead of always using the same fixed cutoff. When the assistant spawns this pruning helper, that chosen limit travels along and is used to decide what gets cut. If no limit is given, it keeps using the previous default. This affects only the internal agent plumbing, so there is no visible change for people using the assistant today.

ai.title: SDK initialSessionState populates fileTree, tokenScores, tokenCallers
ai.summary: SDK `initialSessionState` and `generateInitialRunState` now async, invoking `getFileTokenScores` to populate `fileTree`, `fileTokenScores`, and `tokenCallers` from `projectFiles` instead of leaving them empty. `parseTokens` accepts an optional `readFile` callback to source code from memory rather than disk, returning null-safe empty structures on failure. `languages.ts` adds a fallback `Language.load` path for WASM resolution errors. `@vscode/tree-sitter-wasm` and `web-tree-sitter` added as SDK dependencies.

eli5.text: Starting today, the assistant can build a map of your code project, showing the file structure, how often each part of your code is referenced, and which pieces call which others, right at the beginning of a run, instead of starting with that information missing. This happens when you provide project files through the SDK, so tools and agents that rely on this map now have it available from the start rather than finding it empty.

ai.title: SDK 0.1.10
ai.summary: @codebuff/sdk bumped to 0.1.10. Routine version increment. Only sdk/package.json changed.

eli5.text: You probably won't notice anything different, the engineering team simply bumped the version number of their internal developer toolkit to keep it organized and aligned with other parts they were working on at the same time. This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping, like updating a filing label; no new features, fixes, or behaviors came with it.
